summary: LocalSetup 4.89.4 makes agent work easier to observe, preserves independently owned skills, and adapts test execution to resource pressure while keeping terminal operations under explicit owner control.

highlights.text: **Follow native agent activity:** an owned terminal view shows bounded item metadata and operation state, with guarded recovery after transient read failures and an explicit history-gap signal.

**Keep terminal work under its owner:** managed shell operations retain process and session identity, private input remains operation-bound, and failures provide actionable feedback without granting new authority.
**Use independently owned skills:** select repository, personal, or framework origins explicitly; recorded snapshots and collision checks protect custom source during install, update, and rollback.
**See test pressure and progress:** the shared worker policy adapts to memory headroom and exposes versioned telemetry while the protected test scope retains its resource limits.
**Rejoin the right shell state:** attach, logs, input, and family instructions retain an explicitly selected private state root, including safely quoted paths in older status layouts.
**Find the practical starting point:** the homepage and framework guides lead with visible operations, privacy, and concrete engineering workflows, with detailed mechanisms in linked references.

compatibility: The agent-shell family retained-text contract is qualified for Linux with tmux 3.4. Other tmux versions report an unqualified family result; Windows support remains WSL2-only. Native client activity currently reads bounded metadata from a qualified local Codex daemon, not a complete transcript or a universal client activity feed.

Managed shell mutations require the live native owner's process ancestry and generation. A detached or brokered runner outside that ancestry is unsupported even when tmux is available; use the client's ordinary command tool under its existing permissions and sandbox rather than replacing an owner session.

Explicit private shell state roots remain part of copyable follow-up commands. Omitting one selects the default store and cannot resolve that session. An observation handle does not grant mutation authority.
Independently owned skills keep their source and identity. Discovery or a format check does not trust, execute, upgrade, or authorize a skill; unresolved adapter-name collisions stop before changes.
update: Refresh LocalSetup with its existing install or recorded package-refresh workflow. Run `localsetup shell capabilities` before starting an owned session, then use the actual live agent's qualified owner binding; do not substitute a short-lived helper or an unrelated process.

Select custom skill origins explicitly and inspect their integration-contract status and collision report before updating a target. Preserve local source and resolve changed snapshots through the recorded update or repair path.
Inspect the effective `testing` configuration and `localsetup test-workers --json` before changing worker preferences. Keep test resource controls and the aggregate worker budget in force.
verification: Focused native terminal checks cover activity visibility, layout and input behavior, scoped join instructions, and recovery from transient observer reads while preserving pending items and reporting history gaps.

Focused test-policy checks cover adaptive worker changes, pressure sampling, telemetry fields, and protection of the owned test scope. These checks do not substitute for final exact-candidate validation.

An installed v4.84.6 full-runtime fixture exercised coding readiness and the generated scheduled entrypoint against a synthetic loopback provider. It made three provider requests, read the newly collected granted context, preserved collection during credential outage, and skipped work when disabled. It did not fire a host cron job or use an external provider account; see `ls/docs/LSCLI_QUALIFICATION.md`.

Before publication, require authoritative exact-candidate validation, release-document checks, and signed source and tag evidence. Download the framework archive with its `.sha256` checksum and `.cdx.json` SBOM sidecars, keep all three together, and verify the archive and native-runtime assets. This record does not assert those final gates have passed.
